findings.title: User validation is skipped when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: The authenticated-user check only runs at the end of `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, after an `Integration` row is found with no `OrganizationIntegration`. If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` at line 482 without comparing the OAuth user to the installer. This happens when the installation webhook hasn't arrived or processed yet. An attacker who knows an installation id can then bind it to their own org, which is the attack the PR is meant to stop. The sender is only available once the webhook has created the Integration, so the check is racy and bypassable. The `github_authenticated_user` state is only used in the narrow already-exists branch.

findings.title: Unguarded integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes that `sender` and `login` exist. Integrations created before this change, or by a webhook without a sender, have no `sender` key. Those users would get a 500 instead of the friendly error page. Use `.get` and fail closed with `error(...)` when the sender is missing.

findings.title: Network errors in the OAuth token exchange and user lookup are unhandled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try/except. Only the body read and parse are guarded. A connection error or timeout to github.com raises and produces a 500 rather than the install-failed page. `get_user_info(...)` is also unguarded. The PR says all token failures show the error page, but these paths do not.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The assertion changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request.", and a state-based callback request was added. The test now hits the generic invalid-request error (a state/pipeline mismatch) and never reaches `build_integration`'s 404 handling. The 404 stub is no longer exercised, so the behavior it was written for is untested. The test name is also misleading.

findings.title: No positive test for matching user, wrong state, or failed token exchange
findings.body: New tests cover only the mismatching-user case. There is no test where an existing Integration with a sender matches the OAuth user and the install succeeds. There is no test for a `state` mismatch, for a failed `access_token` exchange, or for a missing `sender` in metadata. In the success flows the Integration doesn't exist yet, so the comparison branch is never exercised. `assert_setup_flow` also relies on the brittle index `responses.calls[2]`.
